messages:
nina (support): FYI customer AcmeMaps reported a big p99 spike on Dedicated eu-west-1 at ~09:08. They said tail latency shot to ~8-10s. Opening a thread to triage.

sam (oncall): on it — can you paste an example req id and the model/pool they hit?

nina (support): sample req: req_0a9f3b2c. Model: redwood-large-quant (pinned). Pool: dedicated-eu-west-1-42. They ramped a batch of concurrent requests around 09:06-09:10. Curl we got from them:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" \ \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \ \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-quant","input":"...","dedicated_pool":"dedicated-eu-west-1-42"}'
```

nina (support): they also attached server-side logs showing a few requests timing out client-side after 6-10s.

sam (oncall): grabbing metrics now.

alex (sre): looking at infra metrics — autoscaler triggered scale-ups starting 09:06:40. Provisioning queue backlog peaked ~09:09 with ~120 pending attaches. p95 is fine (~450ms) but p99 jumped to 8.2s between 09:08-09:22. Kube events show long `ContainerCreating` times; nodes launched but pod scheduling/attach delayed. I see repeated `AttachVolume` style errors in our abstraction: `gpu-attach-timeout` and a flurry of `ImagePullBackOff` on new nodes.

maria (runtime): digging into node logs, sequence looks like: VM allocated 09:06:42 -> kubelet starts 09:07:10 -> image pull starts 09:07:40 -> runtime init finished 09:09:50. So image pull + driver init took ~2 minutes on some hosts. We also have autoscaler configured with `sequentialWarmup: true` for that pool (to avoid hypervisor OOMs historically) so attach operations were mostly sequential which amplified delay (thundering-herd when client ramps).

alex (sre): interesting — sequential warmup + large image = bad combo. Also pool min_capacity for that pool was 0 (we scale from zero), so first wave pays the cold start.

sam (oncall): any quick mitigations we can do now to reduce customer impact?

alex (sre): mitigations we enacted at 09:18: - manually set pool desired=3 (from 0) to pre-warm GPUs, kicked a rolling pre-warm job -> nodes booting in parallel (hopefully faster now). - enabled routing fallback for that tenant to hosted fallback pool (low-latency but higher cost) for in-flight requests.

maria (runtime): customer confirmed after routing change p99 dropped to ~380ms at 09:25. So fallback helped.

nina (support): AcmeMaps says they saw improvement after ~09:25 and are okay for now but want root cause and fixes.

alex (sre): root causes (preliminary):
- Dedicated pool configured to scale-from-zero (min_capacity=0) for cost reasons -> coldstarts on first traffic.
- Sequential warmup/attach policy serialized GPU driver init and image pulls instead of parallelizing.
- Runtime image is large (200+MB layers) and not cached on hosts in that region which increased image pull time.
- Autoscaler backoff/cooldown settings allowed a growing provisioning queue instead of preemptively pre-warming.

maria (runtime): repro steps for engineering:
1) Create a dedicated pool with `min_capacity=0` and `sequentialWarmup=true` in eu-west-1.
2) Pin model redwood-large-quant and send ~150 concurrent cold requests within 60s.
3) Observe scale-up starts but p99 spikes 6-12s due to `ImagePullBackOff`/`gpu-attach-timeout`.

Logs (scrubbed):
```
[09:07:40] kubelet: Pulling image redwood/runtime:large-2026.02
[09:08:15] kubelet: Started container runtime-init
[09:09:52] runtime: GPU driver init completed
[09:09:53] runtime: KV-cache warmup skipped (cold start)
[09:10:02] api: request req_0a9f3b2c served, latency=8.12s
```

sam (oncall): ops-runbook-bot, attach relevant runbook?

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: Dedicated pool coldstart & autoscale (https://internal.docs/runbooks/dedicated-coldstart). Steps: warmup pool, route to fallback, increase min_capacity.

alex (sre): proposed short-term fixes (today/tomorrow):
- Update pool min_capacity for top-tier customers to >=2 (owner: sam, ETA: today, low-risk).
- Add jittered parallel attach: set `sequentialWarmup=false` for pools with >=2 desired nodes (owner: maria, ETA: 48h to QA).
- Make hosted fallback routing aggressive for p99 > 2s (owner: alex, ETA: today).
- Push image size reduction and prepare node image cache warmers (owner: runtime team, ETA: 2w).

maria (runtime): longer-term: implement prefetch layer that ensures runtime image cached on nodes used for Dedicated (requires infra work), and add pre-warm policy keyed by customer SLA (min_warm_buffer). Also plan autoscaler improvements to detect thundering-herd patterns (queue depth spike) and pre-provision.

nina (support): I'll send a status note to AcmeMaps summarizing mitigations and ETA for permanent fixes.

alex (sre): I've filed an incident ticket and assigned a postmortem: INC-2070012345. Will include timelines and metrics. Action items:
- sam: set min_capacity>=2 for AcmeMaps pool, confirm change and monitor (done by 10:00).
- maria: prototype parallel attach flag and run in canary (48h).
- runtime team: image slimming + node cache plan (2w).
- alex: add quick dashboard for provision-queue depth and alert if >50 (24h).

sre-bot: alert archived -> incident INC-2070012345 created and linked.

sam (oncall): I patched the pool min_capacity for the tenant and confirmed 3 warm nodes active at 09:20. Monitoring shows no further p99 spikes for that tenant. I'm leaving a follow-up to make min_capacity change automated when certain SLA tag is present.

nina (support): customer happy with the temporary fix, asked for timeline for permanent changes. I'll coordinate comms for the postmortem. :thumbsup:

alex (sre): thanks team. We'll do a short postmortem and a config change to avoid scale-from-zero for pinned dedicated pools unless explicitly requested. I'll open a PR for autoscaler config defaults after the postmortem.

maria (runtime): adding notes to the runbook about image caching and sequentialWarmup caveats.

nina (support): closing loop — will mark customer incident resolved once postmortem ETA shared.

sam (oncall): end of thread for now. If anything new pops up ping me. :white_check_mark:
